A1.justification: Despite the changed title and expanded scope, both PDFs describe the same research on prompt geometry and next-token prediction. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including v1 Appendices A-E and v2 Appendices A-G.

before.justification: V1 reports original measurements of token geometry, shuffling effects and ID-loss correlations on Pile-10K, plus original OPT and Pythia training-checkpoint analyses in its appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original geometry experiments and adds estimator validation, WikiText word-replacement results, safety-classification experiments and analyses of TunedLens entropy.

M1.justification: V2 adds a supervised procedure absent from v1: compute a prompt's layerwise intrinsic-dimension feature vector and train logistic regression to classify benign versus malicious prompts before generation (Section 6). The underlying token-cloud construction, GRIDE estimator and block-shuffling procedure remain.

E1.justification: The Pile-10K study is retained. V2 adds WikiText-103 with random word replacement (Appendix D) and safety screening on three collections named malicious, jailbreak and attack, supplementing attack prompts with benign Pile text. Short-prompt and cross-dataset evaluations further expand the tested input and transfer scenarios.

E2.justification: V2 Table 2 adds evaluated safety comparators: ShieldGemma 9B, Llama Guard 3 (8B), and a classifier using TunedLens entropy. V2 also directly compares GRIDE with ESS and TLE in Figures 2 and 11. V1's ESS comparison numbers were attributed to prior research, and its TunedLens discussion did not constitute an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: V2 changes the reported main GRIDE scale from 2 to 4, although scale 4 was already examined in v1's appendix. New protocols include balanced safety subsets filtered to 500-1000 tokens, 80/20 train/test splits, length and layer truncation tests, dataset transfer, and TunedLens evaluations across additional model sizes. The main Pile sample and truncation remain unchanged. V2 Figure 11 has an unresolved sample-count conflict: 50 in the plot title versus 2244 in its caption.

E4.justification: V2 adds local-density and distance-ratio checks, comparisons across ID estimators, BLEU/BERTScore calibration, word-replacement sensitivity, interlayer and latent-entropy analyses, and safety robustness tests. V1's nearest-neighbor angle, neighborhood-overlap sensitivity and training-checkpoint analyses are removed. The t-SNE and original OPT analyses are retained under revised terminology and numbering.

E5.justification: V1 already reports across-prompt standard deviations and correlation p-values. V2 additionally reports five 80/20 train/test splits and subpercent uncertainty for safety accuracy (Table 2), and averages over 20 random permutations with standard-deviation bands (Figure 10). These are newly documented repetition and uncertainty practices; Table 2 does not provide individual uncertainty values.

E6.justification: V2 Table 2 adds GRIDE accuracies of 0.94/0.92/0.90 and TunedLens accuracies of 0.96/0.65/0.98 for malicious/jailbreak/attack, alongside new length and transfer results. Appendix G adds model-dependent ID-entropy correlations, including negative intermediate-layer correlations for Llama. Several v1 geometric and training results disappear. The logits-entropy correlations 0.43/0.60/0.60 are retained across matching scales (v1 Figure 18; v2 Figure 17), so highlighting 0.60 is not a new performance gain.

T1.justification: V2 removes v1's unit-box softmax-entropy derivation and numerical-integration argument (Equations 11-12), while retaining the Dirichlet-simplex result, harmonic bounds and asymptotic relationship. Its general-density entropy expectation makes explicit an extension already mentioned in v1's footnote. The substantive theoretical change is limited.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes shuffling-related geometry across cosine similarity, ID and neighborhood overlap, culminating in the ID-loss correlation. V2 retains the ID-uncertainty claim but adds central claims of 90-95% safety-detection accuracy, superiority to guardrails and actionable pre-output monitoring. Safety becomes a principal contribution in the abstract, introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning early safety interventions and cross-dataset transfer, discusses short-prompt and estimator limitations, and acknowledges unexplained negative ID-TunedLens correlations in Llama. V1's training-expressivity and Pythia distribution-familiarity interpretations disappear. The new claim of robust transferability is stronger than Figure 5 supports: off-diagonal GRIDE accuracies range from approximately 39% to 69%.

D1.justification: V2 adds estimator implementation references and neighborhood settings, explicitly identifies deduplicated Pythia variants, explains TunedLens feature construction, and supplies safety-dataset access and preprocessing information. V1's NVIDIA H100 with 94 GB memory disclosure is removed. Both versions provide the same code-repository link; a change in code availability is not established.

R1.justification: V2 substantially repositions the work toward practical LLM safety, adding related work on jailbreaks, prompt injection, guardrails and detection. The dedicated mechanistic-lenses review is replaced by a safety discussion, and estimator-related references expand. Updated publication details for retained geometric studies do not constitute new research relationships.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten, and the methods and appendices are reorganized around ID and safety screening. Terminology changes systematically: v1's token-level analysis becomes prompt-level, while its previous prompt-level comparison becomes dataset-level. These naming changes describe retained constructions rather than new ones.

P2.justification: V2 adds semantic-calibration and safety tables, density diagnostics, estimator panels, word-replacement plots, layer-depth curves and transfer heatmaps, while removing cosine, angle, neighborhood-overlap and training displays. Retained graphics are relocated, including the shuffling diagram from Figure 1 to Figure 9 and t-SNE from Figure 19 to Figure 13. Typography, table formatting and figure organization also change extensively.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens support for the original ID findings through additional estimators, assumption checks and an alternative corruption experiment, while making practical applicability testable through safety robustness evaluations. These gains are tempered by new reporting problems: Section 6 claims robust transfer despite Figure 5's 39-69% cross-dataset GRIDE accuracies, and summarizes TunedLens accuracy as 90-95% despite Table 2's 65% jailbreak result. Figure 11 also conflicts on sample size. The stronger validation supports a limited net improvement rather than an unqualified benefit from the expanded scope.
